INTEGRATED SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.

2. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

4. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. watt (W)
   D. newton (N)

5. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

6. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Curved mirrors? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Curved mirrors.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Curved mirrors.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Curved mirrors.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.

8. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Nitrogen gas only

9. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Producers

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.

13. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

14. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Overgrazing continuously

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.

16. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Water always increases oxygen

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Curved mirrors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Structure of the atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
